To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a deep learning model can accurately identify, classify, and quantify foliar diseases and nutrient deficiencies in soybean and can be deployed for rapid, large-area scouting and real-time detection by farmers and researchers.

a deep learning model trained on a large dataset of foliar stress symptoms in soybean can be used to identify and quantify stress severity with high accuracy, and the model can be used to explain its decisions by identifying key features used to make predictions.

a deep learning framework was developed to identify, classify, and quantify a diverse set of biotic and biotic stresses in soybean with remarkable accuracy and that this framework is explainable, allowing for the isolation of the visual symptoms used in the prediction.

the application of deep learning to plant phenotyping, with the aim of developing a robust, explainable, high-throughput, and scalable framework for the identification of foliar stresses and the quantification of the severity of the stresses in a single framework.
developing a framework for accurate identification and quantification of stress in crops that could be used in a variety of applications, including scientific research, breeding, and production.
the development of an explainable deep machine learning framework for rapid, large scale, and accurate identification, classification and quantification of foliar stress in soybean.
